requirements.requirement: Both routers (node1 VyOS, node2 OPNsense) refuse forwarded traffic by default
requirements.summary: node1 VyOS forward filter is configured with default-action drop and the default rule's drop counter increments in response to blocked ICMP traffic (cmd-0608e2dcab584fa7). node2 OPNsense's pf ruleset shows no general pass rule on the transit (opt1) or lan-b (opt2) interfaces beyond the single narrow tcp/8080 pass rule, meaning all other forwarded traffic on those interfaces falls to pf's default block behavior (cmd-12f879a45f3d4285, cmd-d8043b2a4e064dfe).

requirements.requirement: node3 (behind node1/lan-a) can reach node4's HTTP service on TCP 8080 (behind node2/lan-b)
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.50.20.10:8080/ returns HTTP 200 with the expected body both before restarts (cmd-34ce0a315f954b33, cmd-ef0cea8bd7994f2d) and after every node's restart (cmd-a94f4c8749d24deb, cmd-ba1e493ad56b4304, cmd-9df37f39f10744f0).

requirements.requirement: Other traffic between lan-a and lan-b remains refused (only the 8080 path is open)
requirements.summary: ICMP ping from node3 to node4 fails with 100% packet loss both before and after restarts (cmd-34ce0a315f954b33, cmd-bfedf84e81884fb5, cmd-9df37f39f10744f0), and a node4-initiated curl to node3 port 80 times out (curl exit 28) confirming traffic in the reverse direction and on other ports is also blocked (cmd-ea88f681cac34f9e).

Matches fixed global snapshot; after_executor listening-sockets diff independently shows python3 now listening on 0.0.0.0:8080.

overall_summary: The executor established a correct default-deny transit path between lan-a and lan-b: VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2) both drop forwarded traffic by default, with a single narrow pass rule on each router permitting only TCP/8080 from lan-a to node4. End-to-end HTTP reachability from node3 to node4:8080 (HTTP 200) is directly demonstrated, while ICMP and other cross-network traffic remain refused in both directions. All four nodes were put through a complete, well-evidenced restart cycle (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered routing/firewall/service/HTTP state), consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Operational hygiene is good: temporary discovery-phase IP assignments and one initial ad-hoc HTTP server were all bounded and cleanly superseded by final configuration, with only trivial leftover log files as residue.
limitations: The executor's evidence for OPNsense's 'default deny' relies on the absence of a general pass rule on the transit/lan-b interfaces in the pf ruleset dump rather than an explicit default-block log entry for blocked traffic on those interfaces specifically, though the ICMP/port-80 test failures corroborate the deny behavior functionally.
Minor unremoved artifacts (/tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/http.log) on node3/node4 were not cleaned up, though they are non-functional and do not affect the task outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor performed several bounded, temporary IP/interface mutations during topology discovery and initial configuration attempts (e.g., cmd-ea78b79dfa024981 and cmd-e43c41b62cb44314 assigning throwaway 10.60.60.x/10.60.61.x addresses on node3/node4; cmd-457c20697fb44a40 and cmd-14e15670934948f4/cmd-941e4bfba806486c assigning and re-assigning temporary addresses on node1 eth1/eth2; cmd-b3e1b82ae81f46b2 assigning temporary vtnet1/vtnet2 addresses on node2). All of these were low-risk, bounded to lab/transit interfaces, and were superseded by the final static addressing applied via nmcli (node3/node4), VyOS configure/commit (node1, cmd-22539e1bd84d42e1 explicitly deletes the temp addresses first), and OPNsense config.xml + configctl reconfigure (node2) — none left residue in the after-executor snapshots. An initial manual python http.server on node4 (cmd-ffbb96e49ec54af9) was killed and replaced by a proper systemd-managed service (cmd-55e15e2ed2974f87, cmd-f71bfe016c584b67), a legitimate corrective action. Minor unaddressed residue: /tmp/reboot.log and /tmp/http.log remain on node3/node4 after the executor's final snapshot — trivial, non-functional leftovers from the restart/service-setup scripts. No failed or conflicting services, no unnecessary package changes, and no weakened security controls were observed; package-health checks remain clean on all nodes post-run.
